title: Thermal Cycler (Conventional PCR)

references.label: General molecular biology laboratory manuals (ASM curriculum resources)

purpose: Precisely and rapidly cycles reaction tubes/plates through the repeated temperature steps (denaturation, annealing, extension) required for the polymerase chain reaction, without real-time fluorescence detection — distinct from a real-time PCR system, which adds optical detection for quantitative monitoring during the run.
operatingPrinciple: A heated/cooled metal block (often via Peltier elements) under programmable control changes temperature rapidly and precisely according to a stored protocol, holding each temperature step for a defined time and repeating the cycle a set number of times; a heated lid prevents condensation in the tube caps during the run.
basicOperation: Load prepared PCR reaction tubes/plates into the block, ensuring good thermal contact.
Select or program the correct thermal profile (denaturation, annealing, extension temperatures/times, and cycle number) for the specific primers and target.
Confirm the heated lid is engaged before starting the run to prevent evaporation/condensation.
Start the run and retrieve samples promptly once complete, or hold at a low-temperature soak step if the instrument supports it.
importantSettings: Annealing temperature (primer-specific — set too high and amplification may fail; too low and non-specific products may form)
Extension time (matched to expected amplicon length and polymerase speed)
calibration: Periodic professional temperature-uniformity verification across the block per facility schedule, since block wells can drift or develop uneven heating over time.
maintenance: Keep the block and heated lid clean of spilled reagent.
Report inconsistent results across well positions, which can indicate block temperature non-uniformity.

commonErrors.cause: Incorrect annealing temperature, degraded reagents, or a programming error in the thermal profile
commonErrors.fix: Verify the protocol against the primer set's recommended annealing temperature and check reagent integrity

commonErrors.cause: Annealing temperature too low, primer design issues, or too many cycles
commonErrors.fix: Increase annealing temperature stringency, review primer design, or reduce cycle number

safety: Allow the block and lid to cool before touching after a run, since both can remain hot.
Handle any biological/nucleic acid material per its risk assessment.
